headline: Nscale and Anthropic reportedly in talks for another $45B compute deal
summary: Just a month after a $45 billion compute deal, AI infrastructure provider Nscale and Anthropic are reportedly negotiating a second deal of the same magnitude.
details: A little over a month ago, Anthropic and AI infrastructure provider Nscale announced a $45 billion compute deal. Now, the duo may be about to do it again, with Bloomberg reporting they are on the verge of announcing yet another $45 billion compute deal.

Sources familiar with the matter cautioned that talks are still underway and details could change. If confirmed, this would mark the latest in a series of giant compute deals Anthropic has secured over the past year.

The substantial investment in AI compute deals has raised concerns among some investors about potential overspending for insufficient profit. Despite this, Anthropic continues to pursue such partnerships, confident in future returns.

Both Anthropic and Nscale are also pursuing IPOs, with Anthropic expected to go public this year. Nscale is also seeking an IPO but is reportedly facing investor pushback regarding its proposed $30 billion valuation.

headline_marked: [[Plex Media Server vulnerabilities actively exploited]] to install cryptominers and proxy apps
headline: Plex Media Server vulnerabilities actively exploited to install cryptominers and proxy apps
summary: Recently patched vulnerabilities in Plex Media Server are under active exploitation, allowing attackers to install cryptominers and residential proxy software on unpatched devices.
details: Recently fixed vulnerabilities in the Plex Media Server are under active exploitation. Attackers are chaining four vulnerabilities to achieve remote code execution, installing malware like cryptominers and residential proxy apps.
Plex addressed four vulnerabilities last month, with one rated 8.6 out of 10 severity. A researcher developed an exploit chain, named 'Plex2Shell,' which was later confirmed to be used in the wild.

A separate researcher set up a honeypot, quickly observing active scanning and successful infection attempts. The payloads include cryptominers, which use the device for cryptocurrency mining, and residential proxy software.

Residential proxy apps allow threat actors to anonymize their internet activity, potentially accessing corporate VPNs and emails through infected home IPs. This poses a significant risk beyond just resource consumption.

The exploit chain, developed with significant AI assistance, involves steps like unauthenticated SSRF, security token theft, and payload delivery. Plex users should update to version 1.43.3 immediately.

Users can configure automatic updates or manually install them. Beyond updating, securing media servers is crucial, with the safest option being to restrict access to local networks, though this limits some features.

For internet-exposed servers, routing traffic through a reverse proxy instead of the default port 32400 is recommended. Using only secure Plex apps and strong passwords are also essential security practices.
